_readme: DataTap Azure access register — the machine-readable copy of the Paperclip document
"DataTap Azure access register (the allowlist)" on DIG-1674 (document id
7089f97b-9f0f-4b57-be10-26e787ecf583), which Security owns. This file exists so the
rule can be enforced by scripts/az-guard/az instead of remembered.
The guard reads exactly ONE key: authorized_subscriptions. Every other key is
ignored on purpose. An agent that adds "allow_all": true, "denied": [] or a
comment has changed nothing, because there is no key in this file that opens access.
Each entry must be a full subscription UUID. A subscription NAME is not
authorisation and the guard refuses one: deciding that "Datatap Trials" is
non-production means reading DataTap's tenant, which is the act the rule forbids.
EMPTY IS THE CURRENT STATE AND IT IS ENFORCED: an empty list refuses every az
command, including reads. Only DataTap, in writing, can add a row — DIG-1687. When a
row arrives, Security edits this file in the same PR as the document and records
